lessons.title: How do you feel?
lessons.goal: Say how you feel and share good and bad news.

tip.title: être + adjective, avoir + noun
tip.body: Some feelings use être + an adjective that agrees with the speaker: je suis content / contente, déçu / déçue, inquiet / inquiète. Others use avoir + a noun with no article: avoir peur (to be afraid), avoir hâte (to be looking forward to / can't wait), avoir honte (to be ashamed). Both are followed by de + infinitive: J'ai hâte de te voir. Pronunciation: the h of hâte and honte is aspiré, so there is no liaison and no elision (j'ai | hâte, la honte). The ç in déçu is a soft s.

lessons.title: Reacting to news
lessons.goal: Show surprise, joy and regret when someone tells you something.

tip.title: Quick reactions
tip.body: Short reactions keep a conversation alive: Ça alors ! (well I never!), Ce n'est pas vrai ! (no way!), Tu plaisantes ? (are you kidding?), Quel dommage ! (what a shame!). In speech the ne almost always disappears: C'est pas vrai ! J'en reviens pas ! Exclamations rise and then fall sharply on the last syllable: Ça a-LORS ! In gentil the final l is silent: Comme c'est gentil ! sounds like 'jan-ti'.

lessons.title: Comfort and encouragement
lessons.goal: Console someone and give them courage.

tip.title: Soft words
tip.body: To console someone, show you understand (Je comprends ce que tu ressens), take the blame away (Ce n'est pas ta faute) and look ahead (Ça va s'arranger). Courage ! on its own is a very common way to say hang in there. Speak a little more slowly and softly. Note the imperative of reflexive verbs: Ne t'inquiète pas (tu), Ne vous inquiétez pas (vous). Fier has a pronounced r (fi-ère), and fière for a woman sounds the same.

lessons.title: Content que… + subjunctive
lessons.goal: Express feelings about what other people do.

tip.title: Emotion + que → subjunctive
tip.body: After a feeling + que, French uses the subjunctive: Je suis content que tu sois là. C'est dommage qu'il parte. J'ai peur qu'il ne vienne pas. If both parts have the same subject, use de + infinitive instead: Je suis content d'être là (not que je sois). To form it, take the ils form of the present, drop -ent and add -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent: ils partent → que je parte. Key irregulars: être (que je sois, tu sois, il soit, nous soyons, vous soyez), avoir (que j'aie, il ait), faire (fasse), aller (aille), pouvoir (puisse), venir (vienne). Good news for speaking: for -er verbs the singular forms sound exactly like the present (que je parle = je parle), and for many other verbs they sound like the ils form (que je parte sounds like ils partent).

lessons.goal: Follow a friend describing an emotional evening.

story.title: Forty and surprised
story.intro: In Brussels, Élodie asks her friend Thomas about the surprise party for his fortieth birthday.

lines.name: Élodie
lines.t: Alors, Thomas, ta fête surprise, c'était comment ?
lines.n: So, Thomas, how was your surprise party?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Incroyable ! Je ne me doutais de rien. Quand j'ai ouvert la porte, il y avait trente personnes dans le salon.
lines.n: Incredible! I had no idea. When I opened the door, there were thirty people in the living room.

lines.name: Élodie
lines.t: Tu as eu peur ?
lines.n: Did you get a fright?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Un peu, oui ! Et après, j'étais très ému. Mes parents étaient venus de Liège exprès.
lines.n: A bit, yes! And then I was very moved. My parents had come from Liège specially.

lines.name: Élodie
lines.t: Oh, c'est touchant. Je suis contente que ta famille ait pu venir.
lines.n: Oh, that's touching. I'm glad your family could come.

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Le seul problème, c'est que mon meilleur ami n'était pas là. Il était malade.
lines.n: The only problem was that my best friend wasn't there. He was ill.

lines.name: Élodie
lines.t: Quel dommage ! Tu étais déçu ?
lines.n: What a shame! Were you disappointed?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Un peu, mais il m'a téléphoné à minuit pour chanter. Et on va fêter ça ensemble samedi.
lines.n: A bit, but he phoned me at midnight to sing. And we'll celebrate together on Saturday.

lines.name: Élodie
lines.t: Génial. Mais dis-moi, qui a organisé tout ça ?
lines.n: Great. But tell me, who organised all this?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Ma copine, Julie. Elle a tout préparé en secret pendant un mois. Je n'en reviens toujours pas !
lines.n: My girlfriend, Julie. She prepared everything in secret for a month. I still can't get over it!

lessons.title: Joys and worries
lessons.goal: Talk about what makes you happy, what annoys or worries you, and what you're glad about.

culture.title: Reserve, warmth and the art of grumbling
culture.body: In France, people often keep a certain reserve with strangers and colleagues and share their feelings mainly with close friends and family, where warmth is very visible: la bise, long meals, Tu m'as manqué ! Grumbling (râler) is a well-known part of everyday conversation and does not necessarily mean someone is really unhappy. Understatement is common too: C'est pas mal can be genuine praise. Québécois are often seen as more openly warm and informal, switching quickly to tu, and Belgians are known for their self-deprecating humour (l'autodérision). These are tendencies, not rules — people everywhere differ.

free.n: Talk about what makes you happy, what annoys or worries you, and something you're glad someone else is doing (que + subjunctive).
free.hint: Ça me rend heureux de … / J'adore … Ça m'énerve quand … / Je me fais du souci pour … Je suis content que … (sois, ait, vienne, puisse …)
free.model: Ça me rend heureux de passer le dimanche avec ma famille. Par contre, ça m'énerve quand le métro est en retard, et je me fais du souci pour mon travail. Mais je suis content que mes amis viennent me voir le mois prochain, et j'ai hâte qu'ils soient là !
